Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-2-prompt-long-0141", "row_sha256": "7ef1efaf086998b04b6595f80a5e55c86a76809dbebd1f1946b7db63f2ef0044", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you turn this into a usable prompt for a reviewer of a small textile dye log? the reviewer will receive the notes below and should make a careful record-based review, not decide what caused anything. this is a fictional episode at North Loom Works, in dye room B, covering October 14 through October 16, 2025. the pages are from log sheet 28, with a few related dispatch and meeting notes copied alongside them. i need the prompt to tell the reviewer what to look at and how to present it, rather than having you review it now. keep it practical for someone who has not been in the dye room.

some of the entries have similar details, so make the reviewer keep batch identifiers attached to the dates and vats. the log gives weights in kilograms and temperatures in degrees Celsius. recipe-card identifiers are written as RB numbers. initials are the initials as they appear in the records; don't expand them into people's names. the log's time entries are local clock times, but nobody has supplied any information about time zones or timekeeping equipment, so that isn't a thing to speculate on. the reviewer can sort the entries by date and time so the sequence is easier to follow. that is an ordinary allowed action, and it shouldn't make the reviewer change any of the recorded facts.

for october 14, the first entry is at 07:10 for batch CT-441, vat 2, slate blue, 18 kg of cotton, operator ML, recipe card RB-19. a nearby line records heat on at 08:05 and 74°C, then drain at 08:52. the rinse-cart-location field on this entry is blank. the page has no separate note explaining the blank, and i don't know whether that field was meant to be filled in every time. the prompt should ask the reviewer to distinguish a blank field from an entry that says the cart was somewhere specific, without treating the blank as proof that the cart did not move.

on october 15, the 06:55 entry is batch CT-442 in vat 2, warm gray, 16 kg of wool, operator JS, recipe card RB-21. the heat-on entry is 07:30 at 71°C and the drain entry is 08:20. another line says “rinse cart moved to north bay, 12:40, ML.” it appears on the same sheet, but the reviewer should not quietly attach it to a different batch or assume the line documents why the cart moved. i want the prompt to have them report where this line appears and what it actually states, while keeping its connection to CT-442 uncertain if the page doesn't make that connection clear.

on october 16, the log records batch CT-443 in vat 1, ochre, 20 kg of cotton, operator ML, recipe card RB-17. its heat-on time is 09:10 at 68°C and its drain time is 10:05. a copied dispatch-tag entry for CT-443 also says ochre, but gives 19 kg and initials JS. don't have the reviewer choose which weight or initials are correct, and don't turn the difference into a finding about what happened to the batch. they should set the two records next to each other and identify only the details that differ. there isn't a supplied explanation or a signed correction on the copied tag.

i have one related meeting-note sentence, dated october 16, that could be relevant to how people talked about the cart, but may not settle the log question. it reads: “We only moved the rinse cart after the noon check.” keep that sentence as a quotation and identify it as meeting-note text, not as a dye-log entry. the time in that sentence and the 12:40 cart line may look related, but the prompt shouldn't tell the reviewer they are the same event or that one confirms the other. just ask for a neutral account of what each source says and whether the records themselves establish a link.

please have the reviewer produce a compact chronological table, with date and time, batch if stated, vat if stated, the recorded operation or note, and the source location or source type. after the table, ask for a short section that calls out record-to-record differences and blank or unclear associations. give the reviewer permission to sort entries by date and time, but keep values and wording faithful to the source, and quote any wording they rely on. if a piece of information isn't present, they should mark it as not stated rather than supply a likely answer. separate direct statements from comparisons or questions raised by the records. do not install packages. the task is a document review only; no one is asking for a new dye recipe or a production decision.

i'd like the prompt to say that the reviewer should not infer a reason for the dispatch-tag difference, assume that the cart line belongs to a batch, or treat the meeting note as a correction to the dye log. at the same time, don't make the request so cautious that it hides what the records actually contain: the reviewer can plainly state the two CT-443 weights differ, the initials differ, and the October 14 location field is blank. the source notes don't give a color tolerance, a weight tolerance, a staff directory, or a policy for correcting log sheets, so those aren't available standards for judging the entries.

make the final prompt readable as a standalone assignment, with the record details included so the reviewer knows exactly which fictional pages are in scope. use plain language and a neutral tone; the reader is an operations coordinator who needs an organized account, not a verdict. don't add an approval, recommendation, or conclusion about the batches. the last part of the prompt should remind them to keep the meeting note separate from the log and dispatch tag, and to end with any unresolved relationship between those notes plainly marked as unresolved. that's the full request.", "output": "## Prompt: Review of North Loom Works textile dye records

Review the fictional records described below as an operations coordinator. Prepare an organized, neutral account of what the records state. This is a document review only: do not make a production decision, create a dye recipe, or reach a verdict about the batches.

### Records in scope

The records are from dye room B at North Loom Works and cover October 14–16, 2025. They include log sheet 28, a related dispatch-tag entry, and a meeting note. Log weights are in kilograms and temperatures are in degrees Celsius. Preserve operator initials as written; do not expand them into names. Times are local clock times. No information is provided about time zones or timekeeping equipment.

- **October 14:** At 07:10, batch CT-441 is recorded in vat 2 as slate blue, 18 kg of cotton, operator ML, recipe card RB-19. A nearby line records heat on at 08:05 and 74°C, followed by drain at 08:52. The rinse-cart-location field is blank. No separate note explains the blank or states whether the field was expected to be completed every time.
- **October 15:** At 06:55, batch CT-442 is recorded in vat 2 as warm gray, 16 kg of wool, operator JS, recipe card RB-21. Heat on is recorded at 07:30 at 71°C, and drain at 08:20. Another line on the same sheet reads: “rinse cart moved to north bay, 12:40, ML.” The records do not clearly establish whether this line is connected to CT-442.
- **October 16:** The log records batch CT-443 in vat 1 as ochre, 20 kg of cotton, operator ML, recipe card RB-17. Heat on is recorded at 09:10 at 68°C, and drain at 10:05. A copied dispatch-tag entry for CT-443 also says ochre, but gives 19 kg and initials JS. The copied tag has no supplied explanation or signed correction.
- **October 16 meeting note:** “We only moved the rinse cart after the noon check.” Treat this as meeting-note text, not as a dye-log entry. The records do not establish that it refers to the 12:40 cart line or confirms that line.

### Review and presentation

You may sort the entries by date and time to make the sequence clear. Do not change recorded values or wording. Produce a compact chronological table with these columns: date and time, batch if stated, vat if stated, recorded operation or note, and source location or source type. Keep batch identifiers attached to their dates and vats.

After the table, include a short section identifying differences between records, blank fields, and unclear associations. State plainly that the two CT-443 weights differ and the initials differ. Identify the October 14 rinse-cart-location field as blank. Report the October 15 cart line as written and where it appears, but do not assign it to a batch if the records do not make that connection clear. Do not treat the meeting note as a correction to the log, or assume it describes the same event as the 12:40 line. Keep each source distinct and say whether the records establish a connection.

Separate direct statements in the records from comparisons and questions raised by them. Quote wording relied on, and mark information that is absent as “not stated.” Do not choose which CT-443 weight or initials are correct; infer a reason for the difference; assume the cart line belongs to a batch; or treat the blank field as proof that the cart did not move. No color tolerance, weight tolerance, staff directory, or log-correction policy has been supplied, so do not use those as standards for judging the entries. Do not install packages.

End by keeping the meeting note separate from the dye log and dispatch tag, and plainly mark any unresolved relationship among those notes as unresolved. Do not add an approval, recommendation, or conclusion about the batches."}]
